evidence: src/business/logic/GateLog.ts: constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService), but scanned() does `const prisma = new PrismaClient(); await prisma.scan.create(...)`, which skips the injected service
src/business/logic/GateLog.ts: busiestGate() uses this.prisma.scan.findMany() directly, while BoxOffice works through EventStore/TicketStore, so the module mixes two data-access abstractions

src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: admit() calls ticket.admit(new Date()) and this.tickets.markScanned(...), while GateLog.scanned(code, gate) separately records a scan without the Ticket domain check, splitting the scan concept
src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: purchase() and listing() both contain `new Event(d.id, d.title, d.venueCapacity, d.seatsSold, d.startsAt, d.priceCents)`, a duplicated mapping
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module is meant to be the business service layer for ticketing. BoxOffice uses dedicated store abstractions (EventStore, TicketStore) and rebuilds domain objects (Event, Ticket) before applying rules. GateLog.ts doesn't follow that pattern:
(1) GateLog's constructor injects PrismaService, but scanned() creates a new PrismaClient on every call, so it skips its own injected dependency.
(2) GateLog queries raw Prisma models (prisma.scan.create / findMany) directly. There's no store abstraction and no domain object, unlike BoxOffice, so the two files use different data-access abstractions.
(3) The ticket-scanning concept is split across both files. BoxOffice.admit marks a ticket as scanned through Ticket.admit and TicketStore.markScanned. GateLog.scanned separately writes a scan record keyed by code and gate, without checking the Ticket invariant. The scan rule therefore lives in two places that aren't coordinated.
(4) Within BoxOffice, purchase() and listing() each repeat the same code that rebuilds an Event from persistence data (new Event(d.id, d.title, d.venueCapacity, d.seatsSold, d.startsAt, d.priceCents)). That mapping should live in one place.

violations.message: scanned() creates `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the injected PrismaService (this.prisma), which bypasses the class's own dependency.

Uses raw Prisma models (scan.create/findMany) instead of a store abstraction and domain objects. This doesn't match the module's pattern in BoxOffice, which uses EventStore/TicketStore plus Event/Ticket.
GateLog.scanned records ticket scans separately from BoxOffice.admit (Ticket.admit + TicketStore.markScanned), so the scan rule isn't kept in one place.
purchase() and listing() each repeat the code that rebuilds an Event from persistence data. This mapping should be in a single place.
